labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right. The labels are cited in single backticks and no **`label`** appears anywhere in the file. The ledger regex needs **`prefix:name`**; the bold declaration docstring at l.524 does not match it and lies past 4000 characters. Statements checked against the strict theorems. (1) hreg_massAModel has exactly the hreg type of massA_singular_dec25_models, forall_exists_massA_dec25_models_iff and existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 (Xα = MassAModel, DY = massAModelCausality, DX = minkowski 2). A probe elaborated massA_singular_dec25_models hreg_massAModel hiso hcov with the family instance found by instance search. (2) chartIso_models_of_subset_reg is chartIso_model_of_subset_reg at the family, with no extra hypothesis. (3) forall_exists_massA_models_iff is forall_exists_massA_dec25_models_iff with hreg discharged: same two sides, N : Type as in the strict theorem. forall_exists_massA_models_iff_sing has the reduced right side (o, o' ≠ none, source meets Sing). Its forward direction is weakening, its backward direction is hiso_massAModel_of_sing. (4) hiso_massAModel_of_sing does what it claims. o = none gives hiso_row_none, o' = none gives hiso_column_none, a source meeting Sing gives the hypothesis h, and otherwise the source is regular (chartIso_models_of_subset_reg). So (b') over the family reduces to E_κ ⇀ E_κ', κ, κ' > 0, at sources meeting the line. (5) massA_singular_models is massA_singular_dec25_models with hreg discharged. It keeps the full (b') hiso and hcov, both disclosed. (6) notMem_axis_of_isAEChart has no hypothesis beyond the chart and a point of its source, and its argument is sound. If φ q is on the axis, then q is singular (mem_reg_iff, regPart ⊆ Reg), so q is on the line. Restricted to regPart, φ is a ChartIso massiveOf κ → E0.causality (chartIso_of_isAEChart_of_subset_reg with hreg_family κ and E0GX.chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas). The radial curve τ ↦ (τ, polar((t-τ)/2, 0)) is 1/2-Lipschitz, so g(ε/2) ≤ g(s) inside the regular part of the source. Then φ(g s) ∈ J⁺(φ(g(ε/2))), and E0.isClosed_Jplus with φ(g s) → φ q gives φ(g(ε/2)) ≤ φ q. E0.le_axis_iff' (J⁻ of an axis point lies on the axis) puts φ(g(ε/2)) on the axis, against its regularity. The reverse direction (source_subset_reg_of_isAEChart_e0_massive) applies the lemma to ψ.symm at ψ p, with left_inv. Both directions are right and cover E_{2π} as well. (7) The witnesses smuggle no hypothesis. massA_dec25_models_e0, isAtlasCausalityDEC25_e0, e0_witness, e0_unique_witness, epi_witness, isAtlasCausalityDEC25_model_iff, isAtlasCausalityDEC25_twoPi, isAtlasCausalityDEC25_minkowski_models and massA_dec25_models_minkowski take no hypothesis. The singular structure at E₀ is E0GX.singularGX and at E_π it is EAlphaGX.singularGX π; both are definitionally the family's values. massA_dec25_e0_manifolds takes only hcov (the definition of an E₀-manifold under DEC-25). Its proof of the cross-type clause is right: a singular x in a chart f into E₀ makes f.symm ≫ e an a.e. chart E₀ ⇀ E_κ, whose source is regular. massA_dec25_models_model concludes only massAModel_facts o. It is a non-vacuity witness for massA_dec25_models_of_isoChartsCover, and its content is isoChartsCoverDEC25_model. Nothing narrower than the paper is offered as an anchor. Every restriction (E₀-manifolds, conditional on (b'), local form at E_π) is disclosed and the row stays partial.

labels.label: cor:massA_cac
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right. The anchors are restrictions, all disclosed. cac holds at every model (massA_dec25_models_model), at E₀ and E_π with their identity X_A-charts (e0_witness, epi_witness), at E^{1,2} over the whole family, and at every E₀-manifold over the whole family with no hypothesis left (massA_dec25_e0_manifolds). For a general E≥0-manifold, cac of every natural causality is already in Causal.Remarks.MassADEC25. Existence waits only on (b') between massive models at the line.

instance.verdict: safe as a global instance; keep it global
instance.details: Probed in the /tmp copy, under `import Causal` plus the file. (a) At a variable o, instance search returns massAModelSingularGX o (rfl). (b) `MassAModel none = E0` and `MassAModel (some κ) = Massive κ.1` hold by `with_reducible rfl`: MassAModel is an abbrev, reducible, and the query is whnfR-reduced before the discrimination-tree lookup. So with no local instance, `#synth SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) (MassAModel none)` fails, and so does the same query at E0. The closer's SCOPE and kb_proposal are correct: the family fires only at a variable index. (c) `massAModelSingularGX none = E0GX.singularGX` holds by `with_reducible_and_instances rfl`. So does `massAModelSingularGX (some κ) = EAlphaGX.singularGXFamily κ`, and so does `= @EAlphaGX.singularGX κ.1 ⟨κ.2⟩` (Fact is a Prop). The TopologicalSpace arguments (instTopologicalSpaceMassAModel) agree at the same transparency. (d) With `attribute [local instance] E0GX.singularGX`, trace.Meta.synthInstance at E0 lists the candidates #[E0GX.singularGX] only. With `EAlphaGX.singularGX` plus `fact_pi_pos`, the candidates at `Massive π` are #[EAlphaGX.singularGX] only. The global family is not even a candidate at a fixed model, so it cannot be ambiguous there. With those local instances, `MassAModel none` resolves to E0GX.singularGX, equal to the family's value at instances transparency, and a variable o still resolves to the family. (e) The strict library has one other global SingularGXStructure instance, opensSingularGXStructure, keyed on ↥U. It does not overlap. lineSingularGX, minkowskiSingularGX, twoLinesSingularGX, E0GX.singularGX, EAlphaGX.singularGX and singularGXFamily are all local-instance abbrevs, and SingularGXStructure.ofHasGroupoid is a reducible def, not an instance. (f) Strict statements elaborate unchanged under the probe: E0GX.sing_nonempty, E0GX.reg_eq, E0GX.sing_eq (at MassAModel none), SFALocalE0.existsUnique_isE0Natural, BPrimeE0.chartIso_of_isAEChart, and BPrimeE0.hiso_massAModel_none rfl with no (inst := …), which is now filled by instance search. (g) No strict module imports the new file. After graduation only the root Causal.lean, hence scripts/AxiomSweep.lean, and future importers see the instance. In a module that carries its own `[∀ o, SingularGXStructure _ _ (MassAModel o)]` variable, as MassADEC25's sections do, the local instance takes priority, which is shadowing and not ambiguity. The instance is named, so curation can list it (kb/0015 item 5). It should stay a global instance: it is what fills the instance arguments of the four MassADEC25 theorems for the planned downstream targets. Demoting it to a def with `attribute [local instance]` would gain nothing.

findings_review.notes: Proved (notMem_axis_of_isAEChart, chartIso_models_none_some / _some_none, hiso_row_none, hiso_column_none) in the readings OQ-34/35, OQ-64, OQ-82. The citation of prop:isom (BTZ_1.tex:378–383) is right. α = 0 or β = 0 with α ≠ β forces a contradiction for a connected U containing a singular point; for E_{2π} → E₀, apply it to the inverse with α = 0. findings_review.finding: All three corollaries hold for E₀-manifolds over every model; the natural causality is the same for A = {0} and A = [0,∞) (l.1501–1504).

findings_review.notes: massA_dec25_e0_manifolds states existence, uniqueness, cac and push-up over the whole family. No Lean declaration states the equality of the two causalities. It follows in a few lines from the statements, and a probe checked this: any C₀ with the A = {0} properties of existsUnique_causality_e0 satisfies IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over the family, so the uniqueness clause of massA_dec25_e0_manifolds gives C₀ = C, which is natural over the family. The finding should say « derivable from the uniqueness clause » or cite a corollary, if one is added.

findings_review.finding: What existence still owes is exactly prop:isom at α, β > 0.
findings_review.notes: The Lean iff (forall_exists_massA_models_iff_sing) is with (b') between massive models at sources meeting the line, not with prop:isom. prop:isom at α, β > 0 (α ≠ 2π), together with the elements of Isom(E_α) being causal isomorphisms, implies that case. The converse does not hold. The REPORT's « This is prop:isom » is an overstatement and should be reworded (see the findings below).
